title: Parthenolide accelerates diabetic wound healing through the STAT3 and TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB pathways.
authors: Song, Dan; Zeng, Zhuo; Tang, Hui; Chen, Kaiqi; Li, JiaMin; Liang, Yi; Lei, Xia; Liu, Hong
one_liner_zh: 该文研究小白菊内酯通过STAT3和TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB通路促进糖尿病伤口愈合，仅涉及分子对接靶点预测，无蛋白质-DNA互作体系、结合建模或AI/物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Diabetic wounds, a common complication of diabetes, can elicit intricate inflammatory responses and progressive tissue damage without proper treatment. Parthenolide (PTL), a natural compound isolated from the medicinal plant feverfew (Tanacetum balsamita), possesses antitumor, anti-inflammatory, and antioxidant properties. This study seeks to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which PTL promotes diabetic wound healing. Using network pharmacology and molecular docking, we identified TNF-alpha and STAT3 as potential targets of PTL. In diabetic mouse models, PTL promoted wound healing with a distinct dose-dependent effect. Both 100 microM and 200 microM PTL significantly accelerated mouse wound repair, while 50 microM PTL failed to exert stable therapeutic effects, likely due to insufficient concentration. Histological and immunological staining assays confirmed that PTL promoted wound healing by enhancing keratinocyte proliferation, angiogenesis, and the conversion of macrophages to the M2 type. Furthermore, in vitro experiments were carried out by stimulating RAW264.7 macrophages with LPS. Through CCK-8 assays, immunofluorescence staining, and Western blotting, we further demonstrated that PTL might modulate the STAT3 and TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB signalling pathways, as well as regulate phenotypic switching of macrophages in the inflammatory microenvironment. Collectively, PTL promotes wound healing in diabetic conditions, a mechanism that may be mediated by the regulation of the STAT3 and TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB signalling pathways and the facilitation of macrophage phenotypic switching to the M2 phenotype to modulate wound-site inflammatory responses. Thus, PTL emerges as a potential therapeutic candidate for improving the healing of diabetic wounds.
abstract_zh: 糖尿病创面作为糖尿病的常见并发症，若未得到适当治疗，可引发复杂的炎症反应和进行性组织损伤。小白菊内酯（Parthenolide, PTL），一种从药用植物小白菊（Tanacetum balsamita）中分离的天然化合物，具有抗肿瘤、抗炎和抗氧化特性。本研究旨在阐明PTL促进糖尿病创面愈合的分子机制。通过网络药理学和分子对接，我们确定了TNF-alpha和STAT3为PTL的潜在靶点。在糖尿病小鼠模型中，PTL以明显的剂量依赖性效应促进创面愈合。100微摩尔和200微摩尔的PTL均显著加速小鼠创面修复，而50微摩尔的PTL未能发挥稳定的治疗效果，可能归因于浓度不足。组织学和免疫学染色实验证实，PTL通过增强角质细胞增殖、血管生成以及巨噬细胞向M2型转化来促进创面愈合。此外，通过LPS刺激RAW264.7巨噬细胞进行了体外实验。通过CCK-8实验、免疫荧光染色和Western blotting，我们进一步证明PTL可能调节STAT3和TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB信号通路，并调控炎症微环境中巨噬细胞的表型转换。综上所述，PTL促进糖尿病条件下的创面愈合，这一机制可能通过调节STAT3和TNF-alpha/NF-kappaB信号通路以及促进巨噬细胞向M2表型转换以调节创面部位炎症反应来介导。因此，PTL成为改善糖尿病创面愈合的潜在治疗候选药物。
